title: Runbook: SSL and HTTP-tunnel block outcomes (bad SSL record, undecryptable traffic, server probe failure, domain fronting, HTTP tunnel)
aliases: Blocked due to bad SSL record
Blocked due to server probe failure
Access denied due to domain fronting
Not allowed to use HTTP tunnel

prose.label: Undecryptable traffic.
prose.text: {{undecryptable-unsupported-ciphers}} The shorter list for sites that only use unsupported ciphers is in [[zia.ssl-inspection.cipher-suites]]. {{undecryptable-non-web-over-ssl}} {{undecryptable-solutions}}

prose.label: HTTP tunnel.
prose.text: {{http-tunnel-block}} Which ports the control blocks is in dispute {{divergence:tunnel-ports-fixed-vs-defined}}, and so is whether PAC is transparent {{divergence:pac-explicit-vs-transparent}}. The menu path of Advanced Settings in these pages is in dispute {{divergence:advanced-settings-menu-path}}. {{http-tunnel-troubleshoot}} {{http-tunnel-solution}} {{http-tunnel-firewall-zt1}}

bad-ssl-record-cause.statement: The Blocked Due to Bad SSL Record page describes the SSL connection as blocked due to the forwarding of non-SSL traffic to ports configured for HTTPS Services; Zscaler marks the transaction protocol as Tunnel SSL when some non-HTTP data is sent after an SSL handshake, and the Block Undecryptable Traffic option in the SSL Inspection Policy controls the behavior for such transactions.

quotes: In the following case, the SSL connection is blocked due to the forwarding of non-SSL traffic to the ports configured for HTTPS Services.
Zscaler marks the transaction protocol as Tunnel SSL when some non-HTTP data is sent after an SSL handshake.
The Block Undecryptable Traffic in the SSL Inspection Policy is used to control the policy behavior for such transactions.

bad-ssl-record-pcap.statement: A client packet capture opened in Wireshark showing Data or HTTP rather than Transport Layer Security after TCP confirms non-TLS data was sent on the connection.

quotes: You must collect packet captures on the client using Zscaler Client Connector, and then open the .pcap file using Wireshark.

If you see Data or HTTP or any other sections instead of Transport Layer Security (TLS) after Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) in the bottom pane, then it validates that non-TLS data was sent over this connection.

bad-ssl-record-solutions.statement: For bad SSL record blocks, the page offers a domain-specific SSL Inspection rule with Block Undecryptable Traffic disabled, or, if all undecryptable traffic to HTTPS ports must stay blocked, a Do Not Inspect rule for the domain.

quotes: You can configure a specific SSL Inspection Policy rule for the domain with the option “Block Undecryptable Traffic” disabled.

If your business requires blocking all undecryptable traffic sent to HTTPS ports, you can configure an exemption for the affected domain using an SSL Inspection Policy rule with the action Do Not Inspect.

undecryptable-unsupported-ciphers.statement: The Zscaler service treats a transaction as undecryptable when the website uses one of the unsupported ciphers EXP, DSS, RC4-MD5, RC4-SHA, DES-CBC-SHA, DES-CBC3-SHA or 3DES-CBC-SHA (this page's seven-cipher list); the page's example shows Blocked due to Server Probe failure as the Policy Action and Not Inspected because of undecryptable traffic as the SSL Policy reason.

quotes: Unsupported cipher suites: The website being accessed uses one of the following ciphers that Zscaler does not support: EXP, DSS, RC4-MD5, RC4-SHA, DES-CBC-SHA, DES-CBC3-SHA, 3DES-CBC-SHA.

An example of traffic destined to a website with unsupported ciphers shows Blocked due to Server Probe failure in the Policy Action column and the SSL Policy reason shows Not Inspected because of undecryptable traffic.

undecryptable-non-web-over-ssl.statement: Non-SSL traffic from applications using ports configured as HTTPS Services under Services Forwarded to HTTP Web Proxy is identified as undecryptable.

quotes: The Zscaler service allows you to configure HTTPS Services under Services Forwarded to HTTP Web Proxy. If any applications send non-SSL traffic using the ports configured for HTTPS Services, the Zscaler service identifies such transactions as undecryptable traffic.

undecryptable-solutions.statement: If a trusted domain needs non-SSL communication using HTTPS ports, the page says to configure a Do Not Inspect rule for it or disable the Block Undecryptable Traffic option; for a nonstandard TCP port considered undecryptable, it says to review whether HTTPS applications use that port and update the services configured as HTTPS Services.

quotes: If you trust a specific domain that requires non-SSL communication using HTTPS ports, you can either configure a rule for that domain with Do Not Inspect action or disable the Block Undecryptable Traffic option.

If an application's traffic to a nonstandard TCP port is considered undecryptable, review whether your organization accesses any HTTPS applications over that port and accordingly update the services configured as HTTPS Services under Administration > Advanced Settings > Services Forwarded to HTTP Web Proxy.

server-probe-cause.statement: A server probe failure block applies when the Service Edge cannot connect to the target website by TCP or TLS, which happens when the web server does not tolerate SSL Inspection or does not complete the TCP handshake.

quotes: This happens when a web server either does not tolerate SSL Inspection or doesn't complete the TCP handshake with the Zscaler Service Edge.

This runbook article describes how to resolve a triggered policy action when the Zscaler Service Edge cannot successfully connect to the target website that triggered the policy action via TCP or TLS.

server-probe-eun-decrypt.statement: With the SSL Inspection action Do Not Inspect and Evaluate Other Policies, the error can still appear when the domain part of a URL is blocked in an access control policy, because the service must decrypt a blocked transaction to show the End User Notification.

quotes: If you have selected the action in the SSL Inspection policy as Do Not Inspect and Evaluate Other Policies,

this error can still be displayed when the domain part of a URL is configured to be blocked in an access control policy, because the Zscaler service must decrypt a blocked transaction in order to show the End User Notification.

server-probe-solutions.statement: For server probe failures the page suggests disabling Block Undecryptable Traffic in an Inspect rule for the domain, or as a workaround setting the rule action to Do Not Inspect and Bypass Other Policies.

quotes: you can disable the option Block Undecryptable Traffic in the SSL Inspection rule for the domain with the action set to Inspect.
As a workaround, you can also set the action in the rule to Do Not Inspect and Bypass Other Policies.

domain-fronting-definition.statement: The runbook defines domain fronting as the domain in the SNI extension or Connect request differing from the one later supplied in the Host header.

quotes: In a domain fronting attack, the domain used in Server Name Indication (SNI) extension or in the Connect request is different from the one supplied later in the Host header.

domain-fronting-diagnosis.statement: To diagnose a domain-fronting denial, confirm Block Domain Fronting under Administration > Advanced Settings is enabled, then compare the URL with the Domain Fronted SNI and Domain Fronted Host Header web log columns; a difference means access is denied as configured.

quotes: Validate that the Block Domain Fronting option under Administration > Advanced Settings is enabled and review the exemptions in that section.
Review the values in the following Web Insights logs columns: URL, Domain Fronted Host Header, and Domain Fronted SNI.
If the URL value is different from either the Domain Fronted SNI or the Domain Fronted Host Header values, then the access is getting denied as configured.

domain-fronting-solutions.statement: Zscaler does not recommend disabling Block Domain Fronting because it is a global setting; the page suggests exempting a trusted URL or Cloud App, or a Do Not Inspect SSL rule for a trusted application's domain.

quotes: Zscaler doesn't recommend disabling the option Block Domain Fronting under Administration > Advanced Settings because it is a global setting applicable to the entire organization.
If your business trusts a specific URL or Cloud App, you can choose to add it to the exemptions.
if your business trusts a specific application, you can choose to configure an SSL Inspection rule with the action Do Not Inspect for the concerned domain.

http-tunnel-block.statement: The Not Allowed to Use HTTP Tunnel page says Block Tunneling to Non-HTTP/HTTPS Ports, under Administration > Advanced Settings > HTTP Tunnel Control, is enabled by default for explicit proxy mode, blocks HTTP Connect requests from ports not defined under HTTP/HTTPS services, and does not apply to transparent proxy mode (its examples: IPSec, GRE without Zscaler Client Connector, or PAC file).

quotes: The Zscaler service offers this control using the option Block Tunneling to Non-HTTP/HTTPS Ports under Administration > Advanced Settings > HTTP Tunnel Control.
This option is enabled by default for explicit proxy mode of traffic forwarding. When enabled, it blocks the HTTP Connect method requests from all the ports not defined under HTTP/HTTPS services.
It is not applicable in the case of transparent proxy mode (e.g., IPSec, GRE without Zscaler Client Connector, or PAC file).

http-tunnel-troubleshoot.statement: To check an HTTP tunnel block, find the services forwarded to the HTTP Web Proxy under Advanced Settings, look up their ports in Network Services, and check the Web Insights logs; if the transaction port is not among them, it is correctly blocked.

quotes: Determine the services forwarded to HTTP Web Proxy under Administration > Advanced Settings.
Look up the ports corresponding to these services from Administration > Network Services.
If not, then it is correctly blocked as per the feature Block Tunneling to Non-HTTP/HTTPS Ports.
Review in the Web Insights logs whether one of these ports is used for the concerned transaction.

http-tunnel-solution.statement: Zscaler does not recommend disabling the Block Tunneling option because it is global; instead create a custom network service with the port under TCP Destination Ports, add it under Services Forwarded to HTTP Web Proxy, and add a firewall control policy allowing the port.

quotes: Zscaler doesn't recommend disabling the Block Tunneling option for non-HTTP/HTTPS ports, because this is a global setting and would allow HTTP tunneling to all the ports.
Add a new network service and add the required port under TCP Destination Ports.
Under Services Forwarded to HTTP Web Proxy, add the network service you created to the HTTP Services.
Add a firewall control policy to allow access to this nonstandard port traffic

http-tunnel-firewall-zt1.statement: For firewall rules to apply to remote user traffic forwarded via Z-Tunnel 1.0 or PAC, enable Enable Firewall for Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC Road Warriors.

quotes: Enable the options Enable Firewall for Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC Road Warriors for the firewall rules to be applied on the remote user traffic forwarded via Z-Tunnel 1.0 or PAC.

tunnel-ports-fixed-vs-defined.summary: The advanced settings page says Block Tunneling to Non-HTTP/HTTPS Ports restricts CONNECT requests to ports 80 and 443; the runbook says it blocks CONNECT requests from ports not defined under HTTP/HTTPS services, and fixes a block by adding a network service to those services.

positions.says: The option restricts HTTP CONNECT requests to the standard HTTP/HTTPS ports 80 and 443.

quotes: Block Tunneling to Non-HTTP/HTTPS Ports: Enable to allow the service to restrict HTTP CONNECT method requests to the standard HTTP/HTTPS ports 80 and 443.

positions.says: The option blocks HTTP Connect requests from all ports not defined under HTTP/HTTPS services.

quotes: When enabled, it blocks the HTTP Connect method requests from all the ports not defined under HTTP/HTTPS services.

tunnel-ports-fixed-vs-defined.impact: Whether adding a port to the HTTP Services list lets CONNECT through depends on which reading holds; the runbook's own fix assumes the services list, not the fixed ports 80 and 443.

pac-explicit-vs-transparent.summary: The HTTP tunnel runbook lists a PAC file as an example of transparent proxy mode, while the explicit proxy page describes a browser configured to use a PAC file as explicit mode.

positions.says: The Block Tunneling option is not applicable to transparent proxy mode, with IPSec, GRE without Zscaler Client Connector, or a PAC file given as examples.

quotes: It is not applicable in the case of transparent proxy mode (e.g., IPSec, GRE without Zscaler Client Connector, or PAC file).

positions.says: In explicit mode the browser is configured manually, or with a PAC file, to send traffic to a Service Edge.

quotes: The user either manually configures the browser’s settings or configures the browser to use a PAC file to send traffic to a Service Edge.

pac-explicit-vs-transparent.impact: Whether Block Tunneling applies to traffic sent by a PAC file depends on which page is read; the same runbook says the option is enabled by default for explicit proxy mode.

advanced-settings-menu-path.summary: The runbook pages give the menu path Administration > Advanced Settings, while the XFF runbook page and the July 2026 release summary give Policies > Common Configuration > Advanced > Advanced Settings.

positions.says: Block Domain Fronting is under Administration > Advanced Settings.

quotes: Validate that the Block Domain Fronting option under Administration > Advanced Settings is enabled and review the exemptions in that section.

positions.says: Advanced Settings, including Domain Fronting, is under Policies > Common Configuration > Advanced > Advanced Settings.

quotes: In Advanced Settings (Policies > Common Configuration > Advanced > Advanced Settings > Domain Fronting), there are two new options available under Block Domain Fronting:

advanced-settings-menu-path.impact: The console path to the Advanced Settings options named in these pages depends on which page is read; the pages do not say whether the menu moved or one path is stale.
